The investigation identified a bug in `rich.text.Text.split` where trailing newlines are inconsistently handled when `allow_blank=False`. Specifically, `Text("a\n\n").split()` returns `["a", ""]` instead of `["a", ""]` or `["a"]`, which differs from the behavior of `Text("a\n").split()` returning `["a"]`. This inconsistency can lead to lost newlines when splitting and joining text.

The root cause is the use of a single `if` statement to pop the last element if it's empty, rather than a `while` loop to remove all trailing empty lines, or a more consistent approach aligned with `str.split`.
